patch_description: Introduce a slow, exponentially averaged slope as a stable trend reference and use continuous signed slope coherence to modulate the fast Kalman correction. When the instantaneous Kalman slope agrees with the established trend, nearly all of the responsive correction is retained. When it opposes the established trend, the correction is smoothly reduced rather than accepted or rejected by a binary rule. This avoids abrupt switching behavior and prevents isolated innovation-driven slope flips from producing false reversals, while sustained reversals remain trackable as the slow slope adapts. The existing small-increment deadband remains as a final safeguard.
